## Core Overview
- Primary Purpose: Introduce foundational concepts of Operating Systems (OS), system organization, hardware interactions, execution modes, and resource management.
- Fundamental Themes: The OS functions as a resource allocator and control program, managing hardware resources (CPU, memory, I/O) while providing a secure interface between user software and hardware.

## Key Concepts & Theorems/Formulas
- Computer System Structure: Divided into four components: Hardware, Operating System, Application Programs, and Users.
- Kernel vs System Programs: The kernel is the single program running at all times on the computer. System programs ship with the OS but sit outside the kernel; application programs are unassociated with the OS.
- Interrupt Handling: Hardware or software (traps/exceptions) interrupt normal CPU operation. Control transfers to an Interrupt Service Routine (ISR) using the interrupt vector. CPU state (registers and program counter) is preserved to resume execution.
- Direct Memory Access (DMA): Used by high-speed I/O controllers to transfer entire blocks of data directly to/from main memory without CPU intervention, reducing overhead by firing 1 interrupt per block instead of 1 per byte.
- Dual-Mode Operation: Hardware mode bit protects the OS. User Mode (mode bit = 1) runs user code; Kernel Mode (mode bit = 0) runs privileged instructions. A system call generates a software trap to safely transition from user to kernel mode.
- Multiprogramming vs Multitasking (Timesharing):
  - Multiprogramming: Organizes multiple jobs in memory so the CPU always has work; switches jobs when waiting for I/O.
  - Multitasking: Logical extension where CPU switches jobs so rapidly (< 1 second response time) that users interact with each running program.
- Storage Hierarchy: Arranged by speed, cost, and volatility: Registers -> Cache -> Main Memory (DRAM) -> Non-Volatile Memory (NVM) / Hard Disk Drives (HDD) -> Tertiary Storage.
- Multiprocessing Architectures:
  - Symmetric Multiprocessing (SMP): Each processor performs all tasks and shares main memory.
  - Asymmetric Multiprocessing (AMP): Each processor is assigned a specific task by a master processor.
  - Multicore: Multiple CPU cores located on a single physical chip.

## Exam Takeaways
- Definition of OS Kernel: The core program executing at all times in kernel mode.
- Mechanism of System Calls: Triggers a trap instruction, toggles the mode bit from 1 to 0, executes the privileged service, resets the mode bit to 1, and returns control to user mode.
- Hardware Timer: Used by the OS to prevent infinite loops or process hogging by generating a periodic interrupt to regain CPU control.
- DMA Efficiency: Dramatically improves high-speed I/O performance by replacing byte-by-byte CPU processing with block-level direct transfers.
- Cache Coherency: Critical requirement in multiprocessor and distributed environments to ensure all CPUs read the most up-to-date memory values across multiple cache levels.
